The stock barely moved today, closing nearly flat while oil prices fell on hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East conflict. Over the past two weeks, however, MPC has gained 9.64%—a move driven by the sharp spike in crude prices following Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz that pushed Brent oil above $109 per barrel. As a major refiner, MPC benefits when crude prices rise relative to finished fuel prices, widening the margin it makes on turning oil into gasoline and diesel.

The recent gains also reflect tight refining conditions: US refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with below-average oil in storage (698.56 million barrels), meaning any disruption to crude supply or geopolitical tension that tightens global markets can squeeze margins tighter and boost refiner profits. Today's small decline fits the broader pattern of profit-taking as traders bet that Middle East tensions may ease.
